background_notes.fact: For finitely supported real sequences u,v on a countable set, |sum u(k)v(k)| <= (sum |u(k)|^2)^(1/2)(sum |v(k)|^2)^(1/2). Consequently, for real sequences f,g on Z with finite support and integer h, sum_k f(k)g(h-k) <= ||f||_2 ||g||_2 when f,g are nonnegative; and for a finite set A, sum_{k in A}|f(k)| <= |A|^(1/2)||f 1_A||_2. For the disjoint shell pieces in S001, sum_{j>=0} Xshell_{s,j}^2 = ||x_s||_2^2 for each finitely supported x_s on Z excluding zero.

background_notes.justification: The finite Cauchy–Schwarz inequality follows by expanding sum (u-tv)^2 >= 0 and minimizing in t when sum v^2 > 0; the zero-norm case is immediate. The map k -> h-k is a bijection of Z, so it preserves the sum of squares; restricting a summation set only decreases such a sum. Apply Cauchy–Schwarz to |f| and 1_A for the cardinality bound. Every nonzero integer lies in exactly one shell j>=0, so finite partitioning of the squared norm gives the shell norm identity. These are precisely the inequalities used in the displayed shell bound and in both shell-norm factors.

background_notes.fact: For nonnegative finitely supported arrays A_j,B_j indexed by j>=0, each fixed integer r>=0 satisfies sum_{m>=0} A_{m+r}B_m <= ||A||_2||B||_2. Therefore, with t=2^(-1/2), sum_{ell>=m>=0} t^(ell-m) A_ell B_m <= ||A||_2||B||_2/(1-t). The analogous bound holds for sum_{J>=q} A_J B_{J-q} for each q in {0,1,2}.

background_notes.justification: Set ell=m+r and apply finite Cauchy–Schwarz for each r; the shifted subsequence's squared norm is bounded by the full squared norm. The same argument handles J and J-q. For 0<t<1, finite algebra gives sum_{r=0}^n t^r=(1-t^(n+1))/(1-t) <= 1/(1-t). This finite upper bound already suffices since the arrays have finite support. The infinite geometric sum equals 1/(1-t), as stated in the packet: t^n tends to zero, for example by (1/t)^n >= 1+n(1/t-1). Thus no unjustified rearrangement of an infinite signed series occurs.

background_notes.fact: For fixed nonnegative sequences x_1,...,x_4 on Z excluding zero, let S be the supremum of finite sums of their weighted products over nonzero zero-sum quadruples. If S_M is the sum restricted to all four frequencies having magnitude <= M, then S=sup_{M>=1} S_M. Each truncated sequence has ell2 norm at most its full norm. Hence a bound S_M <= C product_s ||x_s||_2 with a common finite C implies the full bound and the same bound on every subset of quadruples.

background_notes.justification: Each bounded-frequency set of admissible quadruples is finite, so S_M <= S. Conversely, every finite set of quadruples has a finite maximum of its frequency magnitudes and is contained in such a bounded-frequency set; positivity bounds its sum by S_M. These two inequalities identify the suprema. Restriction removes nonnegative squared norm terms and cannot increase the norm. Every finite sum in any subset is also a finite sum in the full set, proving subset monotonicity. This uses the defining supremum directly, without an exchange of limits or conditionally convergent sums.
